'''Graxol Kelvyyn'''<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2016 Topps Star Wars: Rogue One Mission Briefing|cardname=John Coppinger as Graxol Kelvyyn|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/137403/cid/11208727/2016-Topps-Star-Wars-Rogue-One-Mission-Briefing---Autographs-NNO-John-Coppinger}}</ref> was an [[Anx]] who viewed the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] [[podracing]] event from the [[Watto's box|private box]] of the [[Toydarian]] [[junk dealer]] [[Watto]] in [[Mos Espa Grand Arena]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]<ref name="TPM" /> in [[32 BBY]].<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], which includes Kelvyyn's appearance, to [[32 BBY]].</ref> Kelvyyn had [[Color|creamy white]] skin and wore blue and orange [[Clothing|robes]] with a silver [[necklace]] and a high red collar.<ref name="TPM" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|And Jerome was in another character when the Pod Race audience set was filmed, so I got the chance to play Graxol Kelvyyn for that scene. That was nearly five hours in an oven, so it's great fun for a day but I'm not sure how the performers/actors put up with it for weeks at a time!|John Coppinger|<ref name="Interview">{{WebCite|url=https://www.scifinow.co.uk/interviews/star-wars-interview-john-coppinger/2|text=Star Wars interview: John Coppinger|author=Hoare, James|date=2011-09-01|work=[[Wikipedia:SciFiNow|SciFiNow]]|archivedate=20190727180605}}</ref>}}
Graxol Kelvyyn first appeared in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="TPM" /> Both Kelvyyn and [[Horox Ryyder]], another Anx that appeared in ''The Phantom Menace'', were based on a single sketch produced by concept artist [[Doug Chiang]]. The sketch was used by sculptor [[John Coppinger]] to produce a 3D maquette, and as Coppinger like the image so much he made few alterations when converting it, only adding some details and changing proportions.<ref name="Interview" />

As actor [[Jerome Blake]] was busy playing a different character on the day that Kelvyyn's scene was filmed, Coppinger also got to wear the Anx rig, which consisted of the performer standing on twenty-four inch stilts with the head standing thirty-six inches above that of the performer. As this made the character around eleven feet tall in total, director [[George Lucas]] realized that including an Anx in frame with other smaller characters like [[Yoda]] would require the camera to be too far back. As such, Kelvyyn was filmed sitting down for his scene.<ref name="Interview" />

Kelvyyn was first identified in the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] on a card in the [[2016 Topps Star Wars: Rogue One Mission Briefing|2016 Topps ''Star Wars: Rogue One Mission Briefing'']] set released by [[Topps|The Topps Company, Inc.]] in [[2016]].<ref name="Topps" /> The name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used on an action figure set released by [[Hasbro]] in 1999.<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|packtype=Cinema Scenes|pack=Watto's Box|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/episodeicswattosbox.asp}}</ref>
